1. BANKING, MONETARY POLICY & FINANCIAL REGULATION

~28m read

[JUN-001] RBI Relaxes Capital Requirements for Bank Loans under ECLGS 5.0 (Split Risk-Weight Structure)

  • Regulatory Framework & Mandate: Reserve Bank of India issued an amendment to the Master Direction – RBI (Commercial Banks – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025, significantly easing capital requirements for bank loans backed by the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS 5.0).
  • Split Risk-Weight Mechanism:
    • 75% of the Guaranteed Portion: Attracts a 0% risk weight, meaning banks are completely exempt from setting aside regulatory capital against this portion of the exposure.
    • Remaining 25% Exposure: Attracts a concessional 20% risk weight (drastically reduced from standard unrated exposure weights).
  • Settlement Condition for 0% Weight:
    • Banks can avail of the 0% risk weight benefit only if the guarantee claim is settled within 30 days from the date of invocation.
    • If the 30-day settlement requirement is breached, the benefit of the 0% risk weight is revoked, and standard capital charges apply.
  • Strategic Intent: Designed to release trapped bank capital, incentivize fresh liquidity flow to distressed and contact-intensive businesses, and align sovereign-backed portfolio risk with Basel III Pillar 1 norms.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Risk-Weight Split: 0% on 75% of guaranteed portion vs 20% on remaining 25% (a classic matching/statement MCQ).
  • Time Boundary for Settlement: Must be settled within 30 days of claim invocation to retain 0% risk weight.
  • Policy Anchor: Governed under the RBI (Commercial Banks – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions.

[JUN-002] Launch of ARIFAC: National Industry Platform for AML/CFT Compliance with FIU-IND Oversight

  • Genesis & Institutional Architecture: India's financial sector formally launched the Alliance of Reporting Entities in AML/CFT (ARIFAC) as a premier national industry-led coordination platform to bolster Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Combating the Financing of Terrorism (CFT) frameworks.
  • Administrative Secretariat: Jointly managed and operated by the Payments Council of India (PCI) and the Fintech Convergence Council (FCC).
  • Official Regulatory Observer: The Financial Intelligence Unit – India (FIU-IND) participates in ARIFAC in an official observer role, offering high-level guidance, regulatory alignment, and supervisory coordination.
  • Universal Membership Base: Encompasses all reporting entities regulated under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA):
    • Commercial Banks and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs).
    • Payment System Operators (PSOs) and Payment Aggregators (PAs).
    • Securities market intermediaries, Mutual Funds, and Depository Participants.
    • Insurance companies and Virtual Digital Asset (VDA) service providers.
  • Operational Focus: Standardizing suspicious transaction reporting (STR) formats, conducting joint capacity-building certifications, and creating early-warning networks to intercept financial mule rings.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Joint Secretariat: Payments Council of India (PCI) + Fintech Convergence Council (FCC) (NOT IBA alone).
  • Observer Agency: FIU-IND (Financial Intelligence Unit – India).
  • Legislative Anchor: Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002.

[JUN-003] Credit Guarantee Scheme for Microfinance Institutions 2.0 (CGSMFI-2.0): Expansion to ₹20,000 Crore Pool

  • Framework Evolution: Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services – DFS) and NCGTC operationalized CGSMFI-2.0, transitioning from emergency COVID-era relief (launched 28 June 2021) into a permanent, risk-based, tier-structured credit enhancement framework.
  • Pool Size & Validity:
    • Total guarantee pool expanded to ₹20,000 crore.
    • Extended validity up to 31 August 2026 (or until the ₹20,000 Cr guarantees are fully exhausted).
  • NCGTC Institutional Profile:
    • Implemented by National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company Limited (NCGTC), set up under DFS, Ministry of Finance (established in Union Budget 2013-14; incorporated 28 March 2014 under Companies Act 1956; paid-up capital ₹10 crore; Headquartered in Mumbai).
  • Three-Tier MFI Classification & Loan Limits:
    • Small-size MFIs (AUM < ₹500 crore): Max loan capacity capped at 20% of AUM, subject to a maximum of ₹100 crore; NCGTC guarantee cover of 80%; mandatory bank allocation of minimum 5% of bank's scheme pool.
    • Medium-size MFIs (AUM ₹500 crore to < ₹2,000 crore): Max loan capacity capped at 20% of AUM, subject to a maximum of ₹200 crore; NCGTC guarantee cover of 75%; mandatory bank allocation of minimum 10% of bank's scheme pool.
    • Large-size MFIs (AUM ≥ ₹2,000 crore): Max loan capacity enhanced upward from ₹300 crore to ₹1,000 crore (subject to 20% of AUM); NCGTC guarantee cover of 70%; eligible for remaining available pool.
  • Interest Rate & On-Lending Structure:
    • Lending Rate to MFIs (MLIs to MFIs): Capped at EBLR or MCLR + 2.0% per annum.
    • On-Lending Rate to Borrowers: Capped at 1.0% below the MFI's average lending rate of the preceding six months.
  • Guarantee Fee & Utilization:
    • Guarantee fee fixed at 0.50% per annum on the sanctioned amount in the 1st year, and on outstanding balance from Year 2 onwards.
    • Minimum 80% of funds must be deployed for fresh microfinance loan assets within 4 months.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Large MFI Max Loan Ceiling: Enhanced from ₹300 Cr to ₹1,000 crore (capped at 20% of AUM).
  • Tier-wise Guarantee Cover: Small = 80%, Medium = 75%, Large = 70%.
  • Interest Spread Cap: Lending to MFIs capped at EBLR/MCLR + 2%; on-lending capped at 1% below average rate.
  • NCGTC Foundation: Incorporated 28 March 2014; initial paid-up capital ₹10 crore.

[JUN-004] RBI Master Directions on Bank Lending to REITs & InvITs (49% Aggregate Exposure Cap)

  • Policy Harmonization: RBI released the Master Directions on Bank Lending to Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs), permitting scheduled commercial banks to lend directly to business trusts under strict prudential boundaries.
  • Eligibility & Asset Composition Norms:
    • Banks can lend only to SEBI-registered and publicly listed REITs and InvITs.
    • Operational Asset Threshold: At least 80% of the underlying assets of the borrowing REIT/InvIT must comprise completed, revenue-generating properties/infrastructure projects that have yielded positive cash flows for more than one year.
  • Aggregate Lending & Exposure Limits:
    • Aggregate Bank Exposure Cap: Total lending across all commercial banks to any single borrowing REIT or InvIT (including its SPVs and holding companies) must not exceed 49% of the value of the trust's total assets.
    • Funding Restriction: Bank loans to REITs/InvITs cannot be utilized to fund underlying Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) that are already facing financial distress or have existing non-performing loans with regulated entities.
  • Risk Weights & Governance:
    • Exposure to REITs attracts a 100% risk weight (125% if categorized as capital market exposure).
    • Exposure to InvITs attracts corporate lending risk weights based on external credit ratings.
    • Board-approved policies mandatory; statutory migration to a comprehensive capital charge framework effective 1 April 2027.
  • Statutory Effective Date: Directions take effect from 1 October 2026 (banks permitted voluntary early adoption).

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Aggregate Exposure Cap: ≤49% of the value of the trust's total assets (NOT 50% or 75%).
  • Completed Asset Requirement: Minimum 80% completed and revenue-generating with >1 year positive cash flow.
  • Capital Charge Migration Date: 1 April 2027; General compliance effective 1 October 2026.

[JUN-005] RBI Master Directions on Authorisation of Payment System Operators (PSOs) — Perpetual Licences & Governance

  • Statutory Authority: Issued under Section 4 of the Payment and Settlement Systems (PSS) Act, 2007, governing entities seeking to operate payment systems in India.
  • Perpetual Validity Regime:
    • All fresh Certificates of Authorisation (CoA) granted to PSOs will carry perpetual validity (eliminating the earlier 5-year periodic renewal requirement).
    • Existing authorized PSOs will be transitioned to perpetual validity at the time of their next renewal, subject to complete regulatory compliance.
    • Non-Compliant Entities: PSOs exhibiting governance or operational deficiencies will receive conditional renewals for a limited period of 1 year only, until deficiencies are fully rectified.
  • FDI & Foreign Investment from FATF Non-Compliant Jurisdictions:
    • Investments from jurisdictions non-compliant with Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards will not be treated at par with compliant countries.
    • Fresh investments from FATF non-compliant jurisdictions must account for less than 20% of the voting power of the PSO in aggregate.
  • Surrender of Certificate & Cooling-Off Period:
    • Surrendering a CoA requires a written application to DPSS Central Office, accompanied by a Statutory Auditor's certificate confirming all customer, merchant, and bank liabilities are fully settled.
    • A mandatory one-year cooling-off period is imposed before an entity can re-apply if its CoA was revoked, renewal was rejected, or licence was surrendered.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Licence Validity: Perpetual validity for compliant PSOs; 1 year only for non-compliant entities.
  • FATF Non-Compliant Voting Cap: Must remain strictly below 20% of aggregate voting power.
  • Cooling-Off Duration: 1 year from revocation, surrender, or application rejection.

[JUN-006] RBI Master Directions on Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) 2026 & Mandatory CERSAI Registration

  • Framework Objective: Comprehensive overhaul of the 2014 TReDS guidelines to accelerate MSME invoice monetization, expand participant categories, and eliminate duplicate factoring frauds.
  • Net Worth Requirement & Transition Timeline:
    • Minimum Net Worth for new entities seeking TReDS platform authorization fixed at ₹25 crore (verified by statutory auditor certificate, maintained continuously).
    • Existing authorized TReDS platforms must ramp up their net worth to ₹25 crore by 31 March 2028 (extended compliance horizon).
  • Expanded Market Participants:
    • Platform now formally accommodates: MSME Sellers, Corporate/PSU/Government Buyers, Financers (Banks, NBFC-Factors, DFIs), Insurance Companies (for credit risk cover), and notified Credit Guarantee Fund Trusts.
  • Mandatory CERSAI Registration:
    • Every assignment of receivables executed on a TReDS platform must be mandatorily registered with the Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India (CERSAI) to legally prevent multiple discounting of the same invoice across different financiers.
  • Re-Discounting Facility: Authorizes secondary market re-discounting of discounted factoring units between eligible financiers to facilitate liquidity optimization.
  • Current Approved TReDS Platforms (5 entities):
    1. Receivables Exchange of India Limited (RXIL) — India's first operational platform (commenced 9 January 2017).
    2. M1xchange (Mynd Solutions Pvt. Ltd.).
    3. Invoicemart (A.TREDS Ltd. – Axis Bank & mjunction).
    4. C2treds (C2FO Factoring Solutions Pvt. Ltd.).
    5. DTX (KredX Platform Pvt. Ltd.).

EXAM ANGLE:

  • TReDS Minimum Net Worth: ₹25 crore; Existing platforms must comply by 31 March 2028.
  • Fraud Prevention Registry: Mandatory registration of assigned receivables with CERSAI.
  • First Live Platform: RXIL (commenced operations 9 January 2017).
  • Total RBI-Approved Platforms: 5 platforms as of June 2026.

[JUN-007] RBI Revamped Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme Directions 2026: Collateral-Free Limit Raised to ₹2 Lakh

  • Comprehensive Overhaul: RBI issued the Reserve Bank of India (Kisan Credit Card – KCC) Directions, 2026, applying to all Scheduled Commercial Banks, Small Finance Banks, RRBs, and Rural Co-operative Banks, taking effect from 1 January 2027 (existing loans continue till maturity/renewal).
  • Enhanced Collateral-Free Exemption Limit:
    • Banks mandated to waive collateral security and margin requirements for agricultural loans up to ₹2 lakh per borrower (raised from the earlier ₹1.60 lakh threshold).
    • Exemption equally covers allied agricultural activities (dairy, poultry, fisheries, animal husbandry).
    • Voluntary pledge of gold/silver ornaments for loans up to ₹2 lakh is permitted and will not be treated as a violation of collateral-free guidelines.
    • KCC loans up to ₹3 lakh secured via hypothecation of crops or assets under formal tie-up recovery arrangements may also be exempted from collateral.
  • Standardized Crop Seasons:
    • Short-duration crops: Standardized strictly to 12 months (period from raising crop to harvesting and marketing).
    • Long-duration crops: Standardized strictly to 18 months.
  • Flexi KCC for Marginal Farmers:
    • Revolving credit facility between ₹10,000 to ₹50,000 designed for marginal farmers (landholding up to 1 hectare) based on land and cropping pattern, without requiring complex cost-of-cultivation documentation.
  • Term Loan Component Repayment Horizon:
    • Investment credit/term loan portion under KCC is repayable within a maximum of 6 years (if asset life/repayment requires >6 years, it must be treated as a separate loan facility outside KCC).
  • Maximum Permissible Limit (MPL):
    • Sanctioned limit based on scale of finance + 10% for post-harvest/household + 20% for maintenance/repairs.
    • For 2nd crop season onwards, MPL is notionally increased by 10% per annum over the previous crop season's limit.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Collateral-Free Limit: ₹2 lakh per borrower (enhanced from ₹1.60 lakh).
  • Standardized Crop Seasons: Short-duration = 12 months; Long-duration = 18 months.
  • Term Loan Under KCC: Maximum repayment tenor 6 years (longer loans must sit outside KCC).
  • Flexi KCC Limits: ₹10,000 to ₹50,000 for marginal farmers (holding ≤1 hectare).
  • Effective Date: 1 January 2027.

[JUN-008] RBI Revamps Lead Bank Scheme (LBS): 60% CD Ratio Benchmark & 3-Tier Governance

  • Framework Background: RBI issued revised comprehensive guidelines for the Lead Bank Scheme (LBS) (first introduced in 1969 following the Gadgil Study Group and Nariman Committee recommendations).
  • Key Administrative Designations:
    • Lead District Manager (LDM): Lead Bank must appoint an exclusive officer as LDM for each designated district (assignment of multiple districts to one LDM barred except in exceptional circumstances).
    • District Development Manager (DDM): Appointed by NABARD in every district to liaise between district administration and financial institutions.
    • Lead District Officer (LDO): Appointed by the Reserve Bank of India for each district to supervise credit flow.
    • SLBC Convenor: Convenor bank in every State/UT must designate an officer not below the rank of General Manager (GM) as SLBC Convenor.
  • Three-Tier Governance Structure:
    1. Tier 1 (Block Level): Block Level Bankers' Committees (BLBCs).
    2. Tier 2 (District Level): District Consultative Committees (DCCs) and District Level Review Committees (DLRCs).
    3. Tier 3 (State Level): State Level Bankers' Committees (SLBCs / UTLBCs).
  • Credit-Deposit (CD) Ratio Benchmarks & Corrective Action:
    • Baseline Target: Minimum 60% CD Ratio for rural and semi-urban branches on an all-India basis.
    • CD Ratio between 40% and 60%: Monitored by the District Consultative Committee (DCC) for step-up improvement.
    • CD Ratio below 40%: Mandatorily reviewed by a Special Sub-Committee (SSC) under DCC, chaired by the District Collector with LDM as Convenor.
    • CD Ratio below 20%: District placed under the Special Category Districts for rigorous monthly monitoring and structural intervention.
    • Similar Special Sub-Committees constituted if Annual Credit Plan (ACP) achievement falls below 100%.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • CD Ratio Thresholds: Ideal target = 60%; Special Sub-Committee review triggered at <40%; Special Category status triggered at <20%.
  • Rank of SLBC Convenor: Not below General Manager (GM).
  • Lead Bank Inception: Introduced in 1969 based on Nariman Committee / F.K.F. Nariman recommendations.

[JUN-009] DFS Launches Common Landing Portal for Unclaimed Financial Assets & UDGAM Convergence

  • Nationwide Campaign: Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance launched the Common Landing Portal for Unclaimed Financial Assets anchored around the national theme: "आपकी पूँजी, आपका अधिकार" (Your Money, Your Right).
  • Institutional Integration: Integrates cross-sector unclaimed funds across multiple regulators into a unified citizen-facing interface:
    • Bank Deposits: RBI's UDGAM portal (Unclaimed Deposits – Gateway to Access inforMation), linking inactive accounts (10+ years) transferred to the DEA Fund (Depositor Education and Awareness Fund, Sec 26A BRA 1949).
    • Dividends & Corporate Shares: IEPFA (Investor Education and Protection Fund Authority under Ministry of Corporate Affairs).
    • Insurance Dues: Bima Bharosa / IRDAI unclaimed policyholders' ledger.
    • Mutual Funds & Pensions: SEBI / PFRDA centralized tracing engines.
  • Search Capability: Centralized search across multiple banking and financial institutions using PAN, Name, Mobile Number, and Aadhaar-authenticated digital KYC.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Campaign Slogan: "आपकी पूँजी, आपका अधिकार" (Your Money, Your Right).
  • Inactive Account Transfer Horizon: Savings/Current/FD inactive for 10 years or more transferred to DEA Fund.
  • UDGAM Full Form: Unclaimed Deposits – Gateway to Access inforMation.

[JUN-010] RBI Annual Report 2025–26: Balance Sheet Surges 20.6% to ₹91.97 Lakh Crore & ₹2.89 Lakh Crore Surplus Transfer

  • Statutory Submission: Submitted by the Central Board of Directors of the Reserve Bank of India to the Central Government under Section 53(2) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 (reporting period: April 2025 – March 2026).
  • Balance Sheet Expansion:
    • Total balance sheet size expanded by 20.6% (an absolute increase of ₹15,71,699.15 crore), rising from ₹76,25,421.93 crore as on March 31, 2025 to ₹91,97,121.08 crore as on March 31, 2026.
    • Balance Sheet-to-GDP Ratio: Stood at 26.4% of India's GDP as of end-March 2026 (up from 23.7% a year ago).
    • Initial paid-up capital of the Reserve Bank remains at ₹5 crore (constituted as a private shareholders bank in 1935, fully nationalised on January 1, 1949).
  • Surplus Transfer & Contingent Risk Buffer (CRB):
    • Surplus Transfer to Central Government: RBI approved a total surplus transfer of ₹2,88,588.45 crore (₹2.89 lakh crore) for FY26 (up 7.3% from ₹2,68,588.07 crore in FY25). Total available balance was ₹2,88,592.45 crore (with ₹4 crore statutory contributions: ₹1 crore each to National Industrial Credit Long Term Operations Fund, National Housing Credit LTO Fund, and ₹1 crore each transferable to NABARD for National Rural Credit LTO Fund and National Rural Credit Stabilisation Fund).
    • Economic Capital Framework (ECF / Bimal Jalan Committee): Mandates CRB within 4.5% to 7.5% of balance sheet. The Central Board approved maintaining the CRB at the upper cap of 6.5%.
    • Contingency Fund (CF) Allocation: RBI made a provision of ₹1,09,379.64 crore (~₹1.09 lakh crore) transferred to CF during the year. No provision was made towards Asset Development Fund (ADF).
  • Asset Composition & Financial Performance:
    • Total Income: Increased by 26.4%, while total expenditure rose by 102.4%.
    • Foreign Assets (70.9%): Foreign investments rose 7.9% to ₹52.68 lakh crore; sovereign gold holdings jumped 63.8% to ₹10.94 lakh crore. Net sale of foreign exchange stood at USD 53.13 billion, yielding net exchange gains of ₹1.69 lakh crore.
    • Domestic Assets (29.1%): Rose 44.9% to ₹22.59 lakh crore. Rupee securities interest income grew 37.7% to ₹1.18 lakh crore.
    • Liabilities Breakdown: Revaluation accounts (+63.4%), Notes issued (+11.8%), Deposits (+11.6%), Other liabilities (+21.1%).

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Total Balance Sheet Size: ₹91,97,121.08 crore (+20.6% YoY growth; 26.4% of GDP).
  • Surplus Transferred to GoI: ₹2,88,588.45 crore (FY25: ₹2,68,588.07 crore).
  • Provision to Contingency Fund (CF): ₹1,09,379.64 crore (CRB pegged at 6.5%; ECF band: 4.5%–7.5%).
  • Section Applied: Section 53(2) for Annual Report submission; initial capital remains ₹5 crore (nationalised Jan 1, 1949).

[JUN-011] RBI Annual Report 2025–26: Currency Management, Counterfeits (FICNs) & Digital Rupee (e₹)

  • Banknotes & Coins in Circulation:
    • Banknotes in Circulation (BiC): Increased by 11.9% in value and 10.5% in volume during 2025–26.
    • Highest Denomination Share: In volume terms, the ₹500 denomination constituted the highest share of total banknotes in circulation, followed by the ₹10 denomination.
    • Coins in Circulation: Total value increased by 11.4%, while volume expanded by 4.5%. Coins of ₹1, ₹2, and ₹5 together constituted 80.7% of total volume and 60.2% of total value.
    • ₹2000 Note Withdrawal Status: As of March 31, 2026, 98.45% of the ₹3.56 lakh crore worth of ₹2000 banknotes in circulation at the time of the withdrawal announcement (May 19, 2023) had returned to the banking system. Facility remains active across 19 RBI Issue Offices.
  • Central Bank Digital Currency (e₹):
    • Total e₹ (CBDC) in circulation stood at ₹771.7 crore as on March 31, 2026.
    • Retail programmable CBDC pilots successfully credited food subsidies to Public Distribution System (PDS) beneficiaries across Gujarat, Puducherry, and Chandigarh.
    • RBI launched the Unified Markets Interface (UMI) to facilitate tokenisation of financial assets using wholesale CBDC (first pilot launched on Certificates of Deposit - CDs).
    • Bilateral cross-border CBDC discussions/MoUs held with Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE); joined BIS Innovation Hub's Project Rialto and Project Mandala (Phase 2).
  • Counterfeit Currency (FICNs) Detection:
    • Share of Detection: Only 2.4% of total Fake Indian Currency Notes (FICNs) detected across the banking sector were detected at the Reserve Bank of India; 97.6% were detected by commercial banks.
    • Denomination Trends: Counterfeit notes detected in ₹10, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, and ₹2000 denominations registered a marked decline; counterfeit ₹500 notes increased by 20.5% and ₹20 notes increased by 47.4%.
    • Currency Infrastructure & Awareness: State Bank of India (SBI) accounted for the highest share of Currency Chests across India. RBI replaced its legacy 'Paisa Bolta Hai' portal with the comprehensive Indian Currency Microsite on September 10, 2025. Print trials of varnished banknotes were conducted at BRBNMPL Mysuru Press.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Total CBDC (e₹) in Circulation: ₹771.7 crore (as of March 31, 2026).
  • ₹2000 Note Return Rate: 98.45% of ₹3.56 lakh crore total value returned.
  • FICN Detection Share: Reserve Bank detected 2.4%; Commercial Banks detected 97.6%.
  • Banknote Value/Volume Growth: Value grew 11.9%; Volume grew 10.5% (₹500 note leads volume share).
  • Largest Currency Chest Holder: State Bank of India (SBI).

[JUN-012] RBI Annual Report 2025–26: Bank Frauds, Supervisory Reforms & Regulatory Modernisation

  • Systemic Fraud Surge:
    • Total fraud amount surged 46% to ₹48,021 crore in 2025–26 (from ₹32,803 crore in FY25), even as total reported fraud incidents fell by more than half to 10,114 cases.
    • Public Sector Banks (PSBs): Accounted for 74.5% of total fraud value (₹35,709 crore across 3,000+ cases; average fraud size ₹6.6 crore).
    • Private Sector Banks: Accounted for 23.7% (₹11,399 crore).
    • Dominant Segment: Loan Advances accounted for 85% of total fraud value (₹40,774 crore across 8,640 cases).
  • Consolidation of Regulations Exercise:
    • To streamline compliance, more than 11,000 circulars and instructions were consolidated into 244 Master Directions (MDs) covering 30 functional areas across 11 classes of Regulated Entities (REs), repealing 9,445 circulars.
    • RBI also released 64 draft master directions across 9 functional supervisory areas.
  • Deposit Insurance & Supervisory Governance:
    • DICGC Premium: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (established under DICGC Act, 1961) maintained a flat-rate premium of ₹0.12 (12 paise) per ₹100 per annum (0.12% p.a.) on assessable deposits; coverage limit intact at ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank.
    • Risk-Based Premium (RBP) Framework: Introduced effective April 1, 2026, establishing a 2-tier risk-based rating methodology (Tier 1: SCBs other than RRBs; Tier 2: RRBs, rural co-op banks, and UCBs).
    • Registered Insured Banks: Stood at 1,950 as of March 31, 2026 (124 commercial banks including 11 SFBs, 6 PBs, 28 RRBs, 2 LABs; and 1,826 co-operative banks).
    • Supervisory Data Quality Index (sDQI): Published on a quarterly basis under Utkarsh 2.0.
    • Co-Lending Framework Revision: Reduced minimum loan share retention by Regulated Entities from 20% to 10%, and extended First Loss Default Guarantee (FLDG) coverage up to 5%.
  • AI Governance & FinTech Architecture:
    • FREE-AI Framework: RBI formulated the Framework for Responsible and Ethical Enablement of Artificial Intelligence anchored on 7 Sutras and 6 Strategic Pillars (26 recommendations: 13 on innovation enablement, 13 on risk mitigation).
    • MuleHunter.ai™: AI/ML supervised model developed by RBI Innovation Hub (RBIH) to identify mule bank accounts in near-real time.
    • Digital Payment Intelligence Platform (DPIP): Established as a collaborative network-level digital intelligence utility to combat payment fraud.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Consolidation of Regulations: 11,000+ circulars condensed into 244 Master Directions; 9,445 repealed.
  • DICGC Flat Premium: 0.12% per annum (12 paise per ₹100); RBP framework effective April 1, 2026.
  • Co-Lending Retention Minimum: Lowered to 10% (FLDG cover up to 5%).
  • FREE-AI Architecture: 7 Sutras + 6 Pillars + 26 Recommendations; Mule detector = MuleHunter.ai™.
  • Total System Frauds: ₹48,021 crore (PSBs = 74.5%; Advances = ₹40,774 crore / 85%).

[JUN-013] RBI Annual Report 2025–26: Monetary Operations, Payment Systems & Organisational Milestones

  • Monetary Policy Operations & Corridors:
    • Policy Corridor: Retained a symmetric policy corridor of 50 bps around the policy repo rate (SDF at -25 bps, MSF at +25 bps).
    • Call Money & Repo Market Timings: Call money market trading hours extended to 7:00 PM (effective July 1, 2025; 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM); tri-party and market repo extended to 4:00 PM (effective August 1, 2025).
    • Liquidity Stance: Average daily net absorption under LAF rose to ₹1.86 lakh crore (from ₹1,605 crore in FY25); SDF accounted for 84.9% (₹2.02 lakh crore) of total absorption. WACR spread averaged (-) 7 bps below the repo rate.
    • External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR): As of December 2025, EBLR-linked loans accounted for 50.6% of floating-rate loans at Public Sector Banks and 89.2% at Private Sector Banks.
  • Payment & Settlement Infrastructure:
    • UPI Volume & Dominance: UPI volume surged 30% YoY, crossing 200 billion transactions; UPI's share in total retail payment transactions reached 86%.
    • Global UPI Footprint: QR-code merchant acceptance operational in 8 countries (Bhutan, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Qatar, Singapore, Sri Lanka, and the UAE).
    • NGRTGS Upgraded to Version 4.0: Built on the international ISO 20022 XML messaging standard; RTGS transaction volume grew 15.7% (value rose 12.9%).
    • Banking Web Domains: Under Phase 1, bank websites mandated to migrate to exclusive .bank.in domains by October 31, 2025.

[JUN-015] RBI Introduces Special USD-Rupee Forex Swap Facilities to Attract Capital Inflows

    1. FCNR(B) Window: For fresh Foreign Currency Non-Resident Bank [FCNR(B)] deposits of 3 to 5 years maturity.
    2. ECB/OFCB Window: For fresh External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) and Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs) raised by AD Category-I banks (maturity ≥3 years).
  • Concessional Pricing & Tenor:
    • Fixed Swap Rate: Swaps executed at a fixed rate of 1.5% per annum (compounded semi-annually), significantly below prevailing market hedging rates.
    • Tenor: Aligned with borrowing maturity, capped at a maximum of 5 years.
    • Operational Windows: FCNR(B) swap window open till 16 October 2026 (deposits mobilized up to 30 Sept 2026); ECB/OFCB window open till 15 January 2027 (inflows up to 31 Dec 2026).
  • Statutory Reserve Exemptions & NOP-INR Relief:
    • Eligible FCNR(B) deposits mobilized under this scheme are exempt from CRR (3.0%) and SLR (18.0%) requirements.
    • RBI exempted swap positions from Net Open Position in Rupee (NOP-INR) limits (which restricts banks' onshore deliverable positions to USD 100 million at end of day), allowing banks to swap up to hundreds of millions without breaching exposure caps.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Liberalisation for Persons Resident Outside India (PROI):
    • Permitted individual Persons Resident Outside India (PROIs) (including non-NRIs/OCIs) to invest in listed Indian equity through the Portfolio Investment Scheme (PIS).

  • FPI Limits under General Route Rationalized:

    • Retained quantitative sovereign caps: 6.0% of outstanding stock in Central G-Secs and 2.0% in State Development Loans (SDLs).

[JUN-023] SEBI Revises Trading Framework for ETFs: Dynamic Price Bands & Pre-Open Auction

  • Regulatory Directive: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) revamped the trading framework for Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), taking effect from 1 September 2026, replacing the rigid 20% fixed NAV price band.
  • Dynamic Price Band Architecture:
    • Equity & Debt ETFs: Initial dynamic price band set at 10%. If touched, a cooling-off period is triggered, followed by phased expansions in increments of 5% up to a maximum of 20%.
    • Overnight & Liquid ETFs: Completely excluded from dynamic price bands.
  • Commodity ETFs (Gold & Silver ETFs):
    • Initial dynamic price band set at ±6%.
    • Expandable in stages of 3% following a cooling-off period, with no upper or lower limit on total price expansions during a trading session to mirror global bullion market volatility.
  • Base Price Determination via VWAP:
    • ETF base price determined using the Volume-Weighted Average Price (VWAP) of trades executed during the last 30 minutes of the previous trading day.
  • Pre-Open Call Auction Mechanism:
    • Introduced a dedicated Pre-Open Call Auction session specifically for commodity ETFs to ensure fair price discovery prior to regular market open.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Initial Dynamic Price Bands: 10% for Equity/Debt ETFs (max 20%); ±6% for Commodity Gold/Silver ETFs (expandable by 3%, no cap).
  • Excluded Categories: Overnight and Liquid ETFs.
  • Base Price Formula: VWAP of the last 30 minutes of trading.
  • Effective Date: 1 September 2026.

  • Multilateral Agrarian Summit: India hosted the 16th BRICS Agriculture Ministers' Meeting in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, bringing together agricultural leaders and policymakers from Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, and newly inducted BRICS nations.
  • Summit Theme: "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation, and Sustainability (BRICS)".
  • The BRICS Indore Declaration — Four Pillars:
    1. Food Security, Nutrition & Livelihoods: Safeguarding global supply chains of staple grains, pulses, and edible oils against geopolitical shocks and trade barriers.
    2. Agricultural Trade & Technical Cooperation: Harmonizing sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) protocols and cutting non-tariff barriers across developing markets.
    3. Regenerative & Climate-Resilient Agriculture: Promoting climate-smart agronomy, organic bio-inputs, and climate-hardy crops (focusing on millets / Shree Anna).
    4. Partnerships for Innovation & Food Systems: Scaling Agri-Tech startups, satellite crop monitoring, and institutional investments into cold-chain storage.

[JUN-036] India-Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA): 99.38% Duty-Free Tariff Lines

  • Bilateral Trade Architecture: India and the Sultanate of Oman concluded negotiations on the landmark India-Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), creating a premier tariff-free trade gateway into the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC).
  • Reciprocal Tariff Concessions:
    • Oman's Market Access to India: Oman granted immediate duty-free market access on 99.38% of its tariff lines, covering 98.08% of total Indian exports by value (under previous MFN rules, only 15.33% of Indian shipments entered duty-free).
    • India's Concessions to Oman: India provided liberalized tariff access across 77.79% of its tariff lines, accounting for 94.81% of imports from Oman (primarily petrochemicals, urea, and industrial raw materials).
  • Negative / Exclusion List Safeguards:
    • Strict exclusions to protect domestic farmers and sensitive industries: Dairy, tea, coffee, rubber, tobacco, gold/silver bullion, jewellery, footwear, sports goods, and metal scrap are excluded from tariff reductions.
    • Eliminated import duties of up to 5% on Indian marine exports (shrimp, cephalopods, and processed fish).
    • Instituted bilateral Tariff Rate Quotas (TRQs) and Minimum Import Price (MIP) trigger mechanisms against predatory surges.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Oman Duty-Free Coverage: 99.38% of tariff lines (covering 98.08% of Indian exports).

  • Partner Country: Sultanate of Oman (Capital: Muscat; Currency: Omani Rial).

[JUN-040] MNRE Operationalizes Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India (GHCI)

  • Framework & Institutional Mandate: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE) operationalized the Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India (GHCI) under the National Green Hydrogen Mission (NGHM), establishing the nation's statutory standard for green hydrogen accounting.
  • Emission & Quality Benchmark:
    • Green Hydrogen is defined as hydrogen produced through water electrolysis or biomass conversion with well-to-gate greenhouse gas emissions not exceeding 2 kg CO2 equivalent per kg of H2 (<2.0 kg CO2 eq/kg H2), calculated as an average over a 12-month period.
  • Mission Targets by 2030:
    • Achieve an annual production capacity of at least 5 MMT (Million Metric Tonnes) of green hydrogen.
    • Deploy 125 GW of associated renewable energy capacity.
    • Mobilize over ₹8 Lakh Crore in total investments and create over 600,000 clean energy jobs.
    • Abate approximately 50 MMT of annual carbon dioxide emissions.
  • Implementation & State Adoption:
    • Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) functions as the Nodal Authority for accreditation and certification.
    • Dedicated Policy States (6): Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Gujarat, and Uttarakhand.
    • Integrated Policy States (6): Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, and Assam.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Well-to-Gate Emission Cap: ≤2.0 kg CO2 equivalent per kg H2 (critical numerical MCQ).
  • 2030 Production Target: 5 MMT per annum backed by 125 GW renewable energy.
  • Nodal Authority: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) under MNRE.
  • Investment Target: ₹8 Lakh Crore by 2030.

[JUN-041] Ministry of Textiles Rationalizes PLI Scheme: Halves Minimum Investment Thresholds in Round 3

  • Policy Recalibration: The Ministry of Textiles announced sweeping relaxations under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles to unlock stalled capital and widen participation for MSMEs and emerging apparel exporters.
  • Round 3 Scope Expansion:

[JUN-042] WPI Base Year Revision to 2022-23: DPIIT Introduces Targeted Mean Imputation for Missing Prices

  • Statistical Modernization: Office of the Economic Adviser (DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce & Industry) finalized the methodology for transitioning the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) from the 2011-12 base to the new 2022-23 base year.
  • Methodological Breakthrough:
    • Replaces the legacy "Carry Forward" method (which duplicated the previous month's price when data was missing) with "Targeted Mean Imputation".
    • Imputes missing commodity quotations using the weighted average price trend of closely related items within the same commodity group, eliminating artificial price stickiness.
  • May 2026 Inflation Readings:
    • Headline WPI inflation recorded at 9.68% (all-India Index at 109.9).
    • WPI Food Index inflation stood at 4.49%.
  • Administrative Anchor: DPIIT Secretary Amardeep Singh Bhatia confirmed the parallel run of the new series before final sunsetting of the 2011-12 index.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • New WPI Target Base Year: 2022-23 (replacing 2011-12).
  • New Price Imputation Technique: Targeted Mean Imputation (replaces Carry Forward method).
  • May 2026 Print: Headline WPI at 9.68%; Food Index at 4.49%.
  • Issuing Office: Office of Economic Adviser, DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce and Industry).

[JUN-043] MHA & I4C Launch GrM & MRM Portals: Faster Unfreezing of Accounts & Automated Cyber Fraud Refunds

  • Institutional Initiative: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) and the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) launched two dedicated digital grievance modules to address unintended hardships caused by anti-fraud operations.
  • Two Core Modules:
    • Grievance Redressal Mechanism (GrM) Portal: Dedicated single-window portal for innocent account holders, traders, and merchants whose bank accounts or funds were placed under lien or frozen during multi-layered cyber fraud investigations.
    • Money Restoration Module (MRM) Portal: Empowers victims of cyber financial frauds to track and request legal refund/restoration of blocked illicit funds directly into their verified original accounts via their 14-digit acknowledgement number.
  • Operational Integration:
    • Anchored to the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS) and the National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930.
  • I4C Institutional Profile:
    • Operationalized in October 2018 under the administrative control of MHA.
    • Governed under Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act, 2000. Headquartered in New Delhi under CEO Rajesh Kumar.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Dedicated Modules: GrM (for lien/account unfreezing) & MRM (for money restitution).

  • I4C Establishment: October 2018 under Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

  • Holistic Island Outlay: ₹72,000 crore overseen by ANIIDCO.

[JUN-054] India's First Commercial Coal-to-Ammonium Nitrate Plant at Lakhanpur & Model Solar Village Pahadpur

  • Clean Coal Gasification Milestone: President Droupadi Murmu and Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone of India's first commercial-scale Coal-to-Ammonium Nitrate Project at Lakhanpur, Jharsuguda district, Odisha.
  • Joint Venture Architecture:
    • Executed by Bharat Coal Gasification and Chemicals Limited (BCGCL) — a strategic public sector joint venture between Coal India Limited (CIL, 51% majority stake) and Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL, 49% stake).
    • Converts high-ash domestic thermal coal into synthesis gas (syngas) to manufacture technical ammonium nitrate, reducing hazardous chemical import dependencies for India's mining and civil explosive industries.
  • National Mission Alignment:
    • Serves as the flagship breakthrough under the National Coal Gasification Mission, which aims to gasify 100 million tonnes (MT) of coal annually by 2030.
  • Presidential Heritage Showcase:
    • Prime Minister Modi announced that Pahadpur Village in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha (the native birthplace of President Droupadi Murmu) will be developed into a dedicated Model Solar Village under the PM-Surya Ghar framework.
    • Simultaneously inaugurated the high-level bridge over the Kathajodi River connecting Cuttack and Bhubaneswar.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Location of First Coal-to-Ammonium Nitrate Plant: Lakhanpur, Odisha (developed by BCGCL).
  • BCGCL Joint Venture Equity: Coal India (51%) + BHEL (49%).
  • National Coal Gasification Mission 2030 Target: 100 Million Tonnes (MT).
  • Model Solar Village: Pahadpur Village, Mayurbhanj district, Odisha.

[JUN-055] Indigenous Garudastra 120mm Mortar System & First 17 Women Cadets Commissioned from NDA

  • Artillery Self-Reliance (Aatmanirbhar Defence): The Indian Army successfully concluded field validation trials of the indigenously developed Garudastra 120 mm vehicle-mounted mobile mortar system.
    • Engineered and fabricated entirely by Pune-based private defence manufacturer Nibe Limited.
    • Field trials conducted at the Infantry School in Mhow, Madhya Pradesh; mounted on a high-mobility 4x4 combat chassis delivering rapid shoot-and-scoot mortar firepower.
  • Historic NDA Gender Inclusion Milestone:
    • The Ministry of Defence formally commissioned the first-ever batch of 17 women cadets trained at the premier National Defence Academy (NDA) at Khadakwasla, Pune.
    • The women officers graduated as part of the 148th Course, having entered the academy in August 2022 following the historic 2021 Supreme Court ruling (Kush Kalra v. Union of India) mandating female entry into NDA under fundamental equality rights enshrined in Articles 14, 15, 16, and 19.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Indigenous Mortar System: Garudastra 120 mm (manufactured by Nibe Limited, Pune; tested at Mhow, MP).
  • First NDA Women Cadet Batch Size: 17 women cadets (148th Course, Khadakwasla).
  • Legal Precedent: Supreme Court ruling on Articles 14 and 16 (Kush Kalra judgment).

[JUN-056] NIXI Unveils Four Digital Platforms on 23rd Foundation Day: IX, myIRINN, .IN Auction & AI WHOIS

  • Digital Public Infrastructure Expansion: The National Internet Exchange of India (NIXI) commemorated its 23rd Foundation Day (established on 19 June 2003 under Section 8 of the Companies Act) by launching four nationwide digital platforms.
  • Administrative Aegis: Functions under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), chaired by MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan.
  • Four Newly Launched Platforms:
    1. Internet Exchange (IX) Portal: Centralized management engine to streamline peering points, optimize routing latency, and scale bandwidth across all operational IXPs in India.
    2. myIRINN Portal: Modernized self-service portal managed by the Indian Registry for Internet Names and Numbers (IRINN) for seamless allocation of sovereign IPv4 and IPv6 address resources.
    3. .IN Auction Portal: Transparent digital marketplace enabling real-time bidding, transparent auctions, and portfolio transfers for high-value premium .in and .bharat domain names.
    4. AI-Enabled WHOIS Screening Platform: Machine learning security gateway designed to audit domain registrant credentials and proactively flag malicious or fraudulent registrations across the .in registry.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • NIXI Foundation Date: 19 June 2003 (Section 8 non-profit company under MeitY).
  • Four Digital Platforms: IX Portal, myIRINN Portal, .IN Auction Portal, AI WHOIS Screening Platform.
  • NIXI Chairman: MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan.

[JUN-057] Extended PMSMA (E-PMSMA) Risk-Sticker Norms & Assam-Nagaland Tripartite Petroleum Accord

  • Maternal Health Risk Categorization: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoH&FW) operationalized upgraded guidelines under the Extended Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (E-PMSMA):
    • Mother and Child Protection (MCP) Card Color-Coded Risk Stickers:
      • Green Sticker: Designates pregnant women with normal clinical profiles and no identified risk factors.
      • Red Sticker: Identifies High-Risk Pregnancy (HRP) cases requiring prioritized obstetric management.
    • Monitoring & Antenatal Sessions: Mandates up to 4 additional PMSMA clinical sessions per month for high-risk cohorts; extends active post-partum digital tracking up to 45 days post-delivery.
    • Provides structured financial incentives to HRP women and accompanying ASHA workers for completing 3 additional antenatal checkups.
  • Strategic Tripartite Hydrocarbon Agreement:
    • The Government of India, along with the State Governments of Assam and Nagaland, signed a tripartite Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to facilitate joint oil and gas exploration in disputed border zones, unlocking stalled hydrocarbon extraction in the Northeast.
  • QS World University Rankings 2027:
    • IIT Delhi emerged as India's highest-ranked institution for the second consecutive year, securing global rank 118th with a score of 65.7 (improving from 123rd).

EXAM ANGLE:

  • MCP Card Stickers: Green = No Risk, Red = High-Risk Pregnancy (HRP).
  • E-PMSMA Post-Delivery Tracking Window: Up to 45 days post-delivery.
  • Hydrocarbon Border Accord: Tripartite between GoI, Assam, and Nagaland.
  • Top Indian Institution in QS 2027: IIT Delhi (Rank 118).

[JUN-058] ₹2,352 Crore Chenab-Beas Link Tunnel Project & Fast-Tracking of Chenab Hydropower Infrastructure

  • Himalayan Hydrological Diversion: Following India's strategic review of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) framework, the Ministry of Power approved a major package of infrastructure projects on the Chenab River totaling nearly ₹2,600 crore, executed primarily by NHPC Limited.
  • Flagship Engineering Project:
    • Chenab-Beas Link Tunnel Project: Approved with a dedicated outlay of ₹2,352 crore in the Lahaul-Spiti district of Himachal Pradesh.
    • Involves the construction of an 8.7-kilometre-long trans-basin tunnel engineered to divert surplus discharge from the upper Chenab river basin directly into the Beas river system.
    • Substantially enhances power generation at downstream Beas hydro stations (Pong, Dehar) during peak summer demand while regulating transboundary river flows.
  • Strategic Context: Maximizes India's permitted run-of-the-river storage rights under the treaty while generating peak clean hydro capacity.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Flagship Project: Chenab-Beas Link Tunnel Project (Outlay: ₹2,352 crore).
  • Tunnel Length & Location: 8.7 km in Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal Pradesh.
  • Primary Implementing Agency: NHPC Limited.
  • Hydrological Function: Diverts surplus water from Chenab basin into Beas river system.

[JUN-059] FCI Expands Farm-to-Depot QR Code Tagging of Foodgrain Bags across AP, Telangana & Odisha

  • Supply Chain Digitalization: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution expanded the mandatory Quick Response (QR) code tagging initiative for all foodgrain bags procured and distributed by the Food Corporation of India (FCI).
  • State Rollout Footprint:
    • Formally scaled across three major paddy-producing and consuming states: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Odisha during the ongoing marketing season.
    • Built upon successful technological pilot validations: the rice QR-tagging pilot conducted in Andhra Pradesh (December 2025 – January 2026) and the wheat QR-tagging pilot conducted in Punjab (April – May 2026).
  • Anti-Pilferage & Traceability Architecture:
    • Each gunny bag is imprinted with a unique encrypted 2D QR code detailing procurement centre (mandi), mill code, moisture level, grain variety, date of bagging, and destination FCI silo/depot.
    • Prevents recycling of PDS foodgrains, eliminates phantom milling, and ensures real-time end-to-end inventory auditing on the Anna Darpan logistics platform.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Expanded States for FCI QR Tagging: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Odisha.
  • Previous Pilot States: Andhra Pradesh (rice) and Punjab (wheat).
  • Administrative Entity: Food Corporation of India (FCI) under MoCA,F&PD.
  • Core Objective: Real-time inventory tracing and elimination of diversion/recycling in PDS.

[JUN-060] National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6): Total Fertility Rate Stable at 2.0 & Rotavirus Coverage at 85.4%

  • Demographic & Public Health Accounting: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare released comprehensive analytical findings from the 6th National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6 2023–24):
  • Demographic Transition & Contraception:
    • Total Fertility Rate (TFR): Remained stable at 2.0 children per woman, securely positioned below the national replacement-level fertility benchmark of 2.1.
    • Contraceptive Prevalence Rate (CPR): Rose from 66.7% to 69.1%, driven by expanded modern family planning availability.
  • Maternal Health & Nutrition:
    • Pregnant women consuming Iron Folic Acid (IFA) supplements for ≥100 days jumped from 44.1% to 54.9%; consumption for ≥180 days rose from 26.0% to 37.8%.
  • Child Immunization & Disease Reduction:
    • Full Immunization Coverage (cards): Scaled from 83.8% to 87.1%; over 95.6% of all vaccinations administered through public health institutions.
    • Rotavirus Vaccine Coverage: Registered a historic surge from 36.4% to 85.4%, drastically curbing childhood diarrhoea.
    • Measles Second Dose (MCV-2): Increased from 58.6% to 71.8%.
    • Prevalence of Acute Respiratory Infections (ARI) dropped from 2.8% to 1.9%; severe childhood diarrhoea declined to 0.5%.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • India's Total Fertility Rate (TFR): 2.0 (below replacement level of 2.1).
  • Contraceptive Prevalence Rate (CPR): 69.1% (up from 66.7%).
  • Rotavirus Vaccine Surge: Reached 85.4% (from 36.4%).
  • Full Immunization Coverage: 87.1% (with 95.6% delivered via public facilities).

[JUN-061] West Bengal Launches 'Annapurna Yojana' (₹3,000/Month) & T-Hub Unveils 'ORBIT' Space Accelerator

  • State Social Assistance Restructuring:
    • The Government of West Bengal officially rolled out the Annapurna Yojana (Annapurna Bhandar Scheme), superseding the erstwhile Lakshmi Bhandar Scheme (instituted in 2021).
    • Direct Benefit Assistance: Enhances monthly financial transfers to ₹3,000 per month for eligible women aged between 25 and 60 years who are permanent residents of West Bengal.
    • Statutory Exclusions: Excludes women in regular government employment, government pensioners, and active income-tax assessees.
  • Space-Tech Incubation (AIC T-Hub):
    • Atal Innovation Centre (AIC)-T-Hub launched the 3rd cohort of its flagship space accelerator, 'ORBIT', inducting 13 deep-tech space startups (taking total startups supported under ORBIT to 36).
  • International Cultural Honors:
    • The Indian Haj Mission under the Ministry of Minority Affairs (MoMA) was conferred two prestigious Labbaytum Awards 2026 by Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Hajj and Umrah at Makkah, recognizing digital innovations including the Haj Suvidha App and Smart Wristband geo-locators deployed for over 1.75 lakh Indian pilgrims.

EXAM ANGLE:

  • Annapurna Yojana Monthly Payout: ₹3,000 per month (West Bengal; ages 25–60).
  • Predecessor Scheme Replaced: Lakshmi Bhandar Scheme (2021).
  • Space Accelerator: 'ORBIT' launched by AIC T-Hub (Cohort 3: 13 startups; total 36).
  • Diplomatic Recognition: Indian Haj Mission won two Labbaytum Awards 2026 (Saudi Arabia).
